[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

In federated delivery models, teams create many agent ideas for overlapping workflows. Without strict capability boundaries, agents become catch-all solutions with conflicting intent and unclear ownership.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Define one bounded business capability cell per agent group, with a single primary business outcome, explicit in-scope and out-of-scope intents, named ownership, and defined handoff boundaries to adjacent capability cells.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- When multiple teams are building agents for the same domain or workflow area
- When an existing agent is growing in scope beyond a single coherent business outcome
- When agent ownership is ambiguous or contested between teams
- When intent overlap between two agents is unclear or unresolved
page_texts.7:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Prevents duplicate capability growth by making overlap visible
- Clarifies ownership accountability at the agent level
- Enables meaningful portfolio hygiene reviews
- Reduces the scope of quality validation per agent
page_texts.9:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Federated AI delivery gives domain teams the autonomy to build agents for their own workflows. Without explicit boundaries, multiple teams may build agents that address semantically identical intents, and single agents may grow to handle unrelated outcomes as teams respond to new requests by extending existing agents rather than defining new capability cells.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The M365 Copilot platform does not enforce intent boundaries between agents. An agent's scope is determined entirely by its system prompt and the configuration choices of the team that built it. Portfolio visibility is limited — there is no native mechanism that alerts builders when their proposed capability overlaps with an existing one.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Agents without defined capability boundaries exhibit these failure modes:
- A single agent handles requests from unrelated workflows, making quality rubric validation and ownership accountability ambiguous
- Multiple agents serve semantically equivalent intents under different names, creating user confusion and duplicated maintenance effort
- No defined handoff boundaries — an agent either attempts to handle all downstream requests itself or silently fails when out-of-scope inputs arrive
page_texts.12:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Domain teams need to deliver fast and may not pause to assess portfolio overlap before building
- Governance teams have limited capacity to review every new proposal for boundary conflicts
- Once an agent is in Production state, restricting its scope is a behavioral change requiring full change control
page_texts.14:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

Define a bounded business capability cell before any prompt is authored. A capability cell has exactly one primary business outcome — not a category of outcomes, and not a workflow area. It declares its in-scope intents explicitly, and it declares out-of-scope intents explicitly. A named owner and backup owner are recorded in the capability contract. Handoff boundaries to adjacent capability cells are defined — specifying which agent handles requests that arrive at the boundary.

The capability contract (required by STD-TEC-AI-001) is the artifact that defines the capability cell. For Differentiate or Exception dispositions, prompt authoring begins only after the capability contract exists and has been registered in the portfolio registry as a new cell entry; for Merge dispositions, the proposed capability is absorbed into an existing registered cell and the proposal is closed.
page_texts.15:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[New Capability Proposal] --> B[Draft Capability Contract\nPrimary Outcome\nIn-Scope Intents\nOut-of-Scope Intents\nOwner / Backup Owner]
    B --> C[Run Overlap Analysis\nvs Portfolio Registry]
    C --> D{High Overlap\nDetected?}
    D -- No --> E[Register in\nPortfolio Registry]
    D -- Yes --> F{Disposition}
    F -- "Merge" --> M[Update Existing\nCell Entry]
    F -- "Differentiate /\nException" --> E
    E --> G[Define Handoff Boundaries\nto Adjacent Cells]
    G --> H[Begin Prompt Authoring]
```
page_texts.16:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Capability contract | Defines the cell boundary: primary outcome, in-scope intents, out-of-scope intents, owner, handoffs | STD-TEC-AI-001 |
| Portfolio registry | Records capability cells and exposes overlap for analysis | STD-GOV-AI-005 |
| Overlap analysis | Compares proposed cell's intents against existing registry before Pilot entry | STD-GOV-AI-005 |
page_texts.17:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. A team proposes a new capability and drafts the capability contract defining the cell boundary
2. The overlap analysis compares the proposed intents against all registered cells in the portfolio registry
3. If high overlap is detected, the team and governance reviewer assess whether the proposed cell should be merged with an existing cell, differentiated, or approved as a justified parallel capability
4. If the disposition is Merge, the existing cell entry in the portfolio registry is updated and the proposal is closed; if the disposition is Differentiate or Exception, the approved capability contract is registered as a new cell entry in the portfolio registry before Pilot entry
5. For Differentiate or Exception dispositions, prompt authoring begins after the new cell is registered; for Merge dispositions, the proposal is closed and further development continues under the existing cell's change process
page_texts.18:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Narrow cell**: a single intent per agent, maximizing testability and ownership clarity at the cost of higher agent count
- **Workflow cell**: a group of tightly related intents that form a single user workflow, reducing agent count at the cost of wider quality validation scope
page_texts.20:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- Portfolio registry established and accessible to all domain teams
- Capability contract template available to all domain teams
- Overlap analysis process defined in domain portfolio governance documentation
page_texts.22:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#phase-1-cell-definition]

#### Phase 1: Cell Definition

1. Draft the capability contract: name, primary business outcome, in-scope intents (specific and enumerated), out-of-scope intents (specific and enumerated), owner, backup owner
2. Run overlap analysis against the portfolio registry
3. If high overlap exists: assess merge, differentiate, or request justified exception; for a Merge disposition, update the existing cell entry and close the proposal — do not register a new cell
page_texts.23:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#phase-2-registry-finalization]

#### Phase 2: Registry Finalization

1. For Differentiate or Exception dispositions, register the approved capability contract in the portfolio registry as a new cell entry; for Merge dispositions, update the existing cell entry and proceed to step 2
2. Document handoff boundaries to adjacent registered cells
3. For Differentiate or Exception dispositions, confirm duplicate risk indicator is set in the new registry record
page_texts.24:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#phase-3-cell-maintenance]

#### Phase 3: Cell Maintenance

1. Any proposed expansion of the in-scope intent list requires an updated overlap analysis and change record per STD-GOV-AI-004
2. Conduct monthly review of boundary drift: intents handled in practice that are not declared in the contract
page_texts.25:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Define out-of-scope intents explicitly — not just what the agent handles, but what it deliberately does not handle
- Assign a backup owner at registration time; ownerless capabilities are a rationalization trigger per STD-GOV-AI-005
- Treat the capability contract as a living document updated via the change process, not a one-time artifact
page_texts.26:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- Defining the primary outcome as a workflow area rather than a single outcome — leads to mega-agents that grow without natural boundary
- Omitting out-of-scope declarations — agents without explicit out-of-scope lists will handle boundary cases ad hoc, producing unpredictable quality
- Registering the capability contract after prompt authoring has begun — overlap analysis loses its value if the build is already underway
page_texts.28:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#standards-alignment]

### Standards Alignment

- [STD-GOV-AI-005: AI Capability Portfolio Hygiene Standard](../../../standards/governance/ai/STD-GOV-AI-005-ai-portfolio-hygiene.md) — portfolio registry, overlap controls, rationalization triggers
page_texts.29:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

- The capability contract must be registered in the portfolio registry before Pilot promotion — as a new cell entry for Differentiate or Exception dispositions, or under the existing registered cell entry for Merge dispositions
- Overlap analysis must be completed and documented for all new capability proposals
page_texts.30:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

- Proposed capability contracts with high overlap require Platform Governance Team review before Pilot entry
- Capability contract scope changes (expanding in-scope intents) require a change record per STD-GOV-AI-004
page_texts.31:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate capability rate | Declining over time | Monthly portfolio hygiene review |
| Boundary-change frequency per capability | Low and stable | Change log review |
| Overlap analysis completion rate for new proposals | 100% | Registry audit at Pilot gate |
page_texts.34:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#scenario-1-new-proposal-with-detected-overlap]

#### Scenario 1: New proposal with detected overlap

A team proposes an agent to summarize project status updates. The overlap analysis finds an existing registered cell that summarizes stakeholder reports, with two shared intents. The governance reviewer and both domain owners determine the intents are distinct enough to support both cells, and both capability contracts are updated to define the handoff boundary between them.
page_texts.35:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#scenario-2-mega-agent-rationalization]

#### Scenario 2: Mega-agent rationalization

An existing agent has accumulated nine in-scope intents across three distinct workflow areas. The monthly portfolio hygiene review identifies this as a rationalization trigger. The domain owner and governance reviewer produce a consolidation plan that splits the agent into three narrow cells with defined handoff boundaries.
page_texts.37:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

Multiple agents in the same domain have overlapping intents with no declared boundaries, producing inconsistent user experience and duplicated maintenance effort. No owner is clearly accountable for the overlap.
page_texts.38:
[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

Each agent has a registered capability contract with explicit in-scope and out-of-scope intents, declared handoff boundaries, and a named owner. The portfolio registry provides a single view of all cells and their boundaries.

[patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-008-capability-cell-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Federated teams build overlapping agents without declared intent boundaries, creating capability sprawl and ambiguous ownership.

**Solution:** Define a bounded capability cell (single primary outcome, explicit in-scope and out-of-scope intents, named owner, handoff boundaries) before prompt authoring, and register it in the portfolio registry; if overlap analysis indicates Merge, update the existing cell entry and proceed under its governance rather than registering a new cell.

**When to Use:**
- New capability proposals in any domain with existing registered capabilities
- Agents that have grown beyond a single coherent business outcome
- When intent overlap between two agents is unresolved

**Key Benefits:**
- Makes overlap visible before investment is committed
- Establishes clear ownership accountability
- Enables meaningful portfolio rationalization

**Implementation Complexity:** Low

**Prerequisites:** Portfolio registry, capability contract template, overlap analysis process

**Related Patterns:** PTN-TEC-AI-009 Contract-First Agent, PTN-GOV-AI-009 Portfolio Rationalization
